root_cause.text: The SCTP cookie parsing path failed to perform complete length/bounds validation on the embedded INIT chunk and raw address list in sctp_unpack_cookie() and sctp_raw_to_bind_addrs(), allowing malformed COOKIE_ECHO data to be parsed past the end of the cookie buffer.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds checks that the INIT chunk length is at least sizeof(struct sctp_init_chunk), that raw_addr_list_len does not exceed the remaining cookie payload after the INIT chunk, and that each address parameter has enough bytes for both struct sctp_paramhdr and its declared length before parsing; the CVE/commit text explicitly says the previous code only checked that INIT did not exceed remaining payload and lacked sufficient bounds checks, leading to out-of-bounds reads in sctp_process_init() and sctp_raw_to_bind_addrs().

intent_record.intent_summary: Add bounds checks for SCTP raw address parameters to reject truncated or malformed input before parsing.
intent_record.what: The change adds two length validation checks before processing each SCTP address parameter: it first verifies that `addrs_len` is at least `sizeof(*param)`, then reads `len = ntohs(param->length)` and verifies that `addrs_len` is at least `len`; on either failure it sets `retval = -EINVAL` and jumps to `out_err`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this prevents the function from reading a parameter header or trusting a parameter length field when the remaining raw address buffer is too short, avoiding out-of-bounds access and rejecting malformed or truncated input with `-EINVAL`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove a redundant end-of-loop reassignment of `len` so SCTP raw address parsing advances using the correct computed parameter length.
intent_record.what: The assignment `len = ntohs(param->length);` was removed from the `next:` section of `sctp_raw_to_bind_addrs()`, leaving the loop to use the existing `len` value when updating `addrs_len` and `raw_addr_list`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the code no longer overwrites `len` at the end of the loop iteration, so pointer and remaining-length advancement use the previously established parameter length value instead of redundantly re-reading it from `param`. This avoids inconsistent or incorrect advancement if `len` had already been adjusted earlier in the iteration.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a new local `chlen` variable in sctp_unpack_cookie() to support forthcoming chunk-length handling logic.
intent_record.what: The local variable declaration in sctp_unpack_cookie() was changed from declaring only `unsigned int len;` to declaring `unsigned int len, chlen;`, while leaving the surrounding code unchanged.
intent_record.how: At runtime this enables the function to use a new local unsigned integer variable named `chlen`, likely for chunk-length handling elsewhere in the function, without changing behavior in this specific hunk by itself.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add stricter bounds checking for SCTP cookie chunk and address-list lengths to reject malformed cookies before parsing.
intent_record.what: The code replaces a single length check on `ntohs(ch->length)` with assignment to `chlen`, then adds three validations before proceeding: it rejects `chlen` values smaller than `sizeof(struct sctp_init_chunk)`, rejects `chlen` values larger than `len - fixed_size`, and rejects `bear_cookie->raw_addr_list_len` values larger than `len - fixed_size - chlen`, all by jumping to `malformed`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this strengthens validation of unpacked SCTP cookie data by ensuring the embedded chunk has a minimum valid size, fits within the remaining cookie buffer, and leaves enough space for the raw address list. This prevents malformed or truncated cookie contents from being parsed past buffer bounds or treated as valid.

consistency_review.core_intent: Add stricter SCTP input length and bounds validation to reject malformed or truncated address and cookie data before parsing.

relevance_review.reason: The changes directly add missing length and bounds validation in SCTP raw address parsing and cookie parsing, matching the root cause of malformed COOKIE_ECHO data being parsed past the end of the cookie buffer.

The change affects SCTP raw address parsing length handling in sctp_raw_to_bind_addrs(), which is part of the vulnerable cookie/address parsing path. Correctly advancing by the computed parameter length is directly related to preventing malformed COOKIE_ECHO data from being parsed incorrectly or past bounds.

This change only introduces a local variable placeholder for future chunk-length handling and does not itself add the missing bounds/length validation in cookie parsing or raw address parsing that caused the vulnerability.

candidates.rationale: This dereferences and interprets the raw parameter header without first validating that enough bytes remain for a complete SCTP parameter header, matching the root cause of parsing malformed raw address data past the end of the buffer.

This parses an address parameter from untrusted cookie/raw-address data before complete bounds validation of the parameter length/content, enabling over-read on truncated or malformed address parameters.

This directly treats data following the cookie header as an embedded INIT chunk header before sufficient validation that the cookie buffer contains a complete chunk header, contributing to out-of-bounds parsing of malformed COOKIE_ECHO data.

This trusts the attacker-controlled parameter length from the raw address list without prior full validation that the parameter header and claimed length fit within the remaining buffer, which is central to the bounds-check failure.

This check validates only one upper bound on the embedded chunk length and is incomplete: it does not ensure the chunk header itself is fully present nor enforce stricter structural constraints needed to reject truncated/malformed cookies before further parsing.

vuln_statements.explanation: This begins parsing the embedded INIT chunk directly from the cookie payload before first proving that the remaining cookie buffer is large enough to contain a complete chunk header, matching the root cause of incomplete bounds validation in sctp_unpack_cookie().

This interprets the next raw address parameter header and dereferences its type field before validating that a full parameter header is present within the remaining buffer, matching the raw address list over-read root cause in sctp_raw_to_bind_addrs().

This invokes parsing of an address parameter from untrusted raw cookie data before complete validation that the parameter body is fully contained in the remaining buffer, enabling malformed or truncated address data to be parsed past the end.

This trusts the attacker-controlled parameter length field to drive parsing progress without first fully validating that the parameter header and claimed length fit in the remaining raw address data, contributing to the bounds-check failure.

This performs only an incomplete upper-bound check on the embedded chunk length and does not ensure that the chunk header itself is present or that the cookie structure is otherwise complete, so malformed COOKIE_ECHO data can still be parsed out of bounds.
